props.heading: Honors & Service
props.description: A dossier for earned recognition, voluntary contribution, leadership, and community-facing work. Each signal is framed with context, evidence, impact, and reflection so reviewers can see not only what was achieved, but what it changed.

props.heading: Achievements are strongest when they show contribution, not decoration.
props.description: The page is organized for selective academic review: earned distinction, sustained voluntary work, leadership behavior, and evidence that can be checked without guesswork.

items.title: Awards and Academic Recognition
items.description: Honors should be presented by level, selectivity, issuer, date, and relationship to Aarti's academic direction.
items.method: Prioritize verified honors first, then group school, regional, state, national, and international signals in a clean hierarchy.
items.evidence: Certificate, official listing, teacher confirmation, competition page, transcript notation, or published result.
items.outcome: Reviewers can quickly understand what was earned, how selective it was, and why it matters.

items.title: Voluntary Work and Community Contribution
items.description: Service entries should explain the need, Aarti's role, the people served, time commitment, and the practical outcome.
items.method: Frame each service item as problem, action, impact, reflection, and next step.
items.evidence: Organization link, hours log, supervisor note, event artifact, project output, or public documentation.
items.outcome: The work reads as sustained responsibility rather than a scattered activity list.

items.title: Initiative, Mentorship, and Systems Built for Others
items.description: Leadership should show where Aarti made something easier, clearer, more humane, or more useful for a group.
items.method: Name the constraint, the decision Aarti owned, the collaboration involved, and the result others could use.
items.evidence: Project links, GitHub commits, writing, meeting artifacts, testimonials from known adults, or shipped resources.
items.outcome: Leadership becomes visible as behavior: initiative, follow-through, care, and accountable execution.

props.heading: The throughline: distinction should leave useful evidence behind.
props.body:
For Aarti's portfolio, honors and service should not feel separate from research and software. They should show the same pattern: observe a real need, take responsibility, build or contribute something useful, document the work, and reflect honestly on what improved.

That is the admissions-grade case: not a long list of impressive nouns, but a consistent record of curiosity becoming contribution.

props.heading: Honors and service FAQ
props.description: Short guidance for keeping the page useful, credible, and ready for future verified entries.

faqs.question: Why not publish a long list immediately?
faqs.answer: For selective academic review, accuracy is stronger than volume. Each item should include enough context and evidence to be trusted.

faqs.question: What counts as an honor?
faqs.answer: Academic awards, subject recognition, honor societies, competition results, research or writing recognition, and other earned distinctions can qualify when the issuer, scope, and date are clear.

faqs.question: What counts as service?
faqs.answer: Volunteer work, mentoring, community support, student support projects, technical tools built for others, and sustained responsibilities can all count when the beneficiary and contribution are clear.

faqs.question: How should future entries be added?
faqs.answer: Use the same pattern for each entry: title, organization, date, level or scope, role, action, impact, evidence, and reflection.
